decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The proposed development at Feltham Airparcs, as shown on drawings 500 PA 01, 500 PA 11, 200 PA 01, 200 PA 02, 200 PA 03, 200 PA 04, 200 PA 05, 200 PA 11, 200 PA 12, 200 PA 13, 200 PA 21, 200 PA 61, 200 PA 62, 100 PA 41 and 50 PA 61; received 7 April 2009 and 500 PA 12 Rev B, 200 PA 21 Rev B, 200 PA 63 Rev B received 26 June 2009 (Amended Plans); to create a new leisure hub including the relocation of the Hanworth Library to the site, as well as refurbishment and floodlighting of the existing tennis courts and upgrading of landscape and carpark areas is acceptable, subject to the safeguarding conditions recommended, for the following reasons.

The proposal would enhance the appearance, accessibility and range of leisure and recreation facilities of the existing community facility. It would incorporate environmentally sustainable measures including energy efficient heat and power systems, 'brown roofs' and rainwater reuse and would have minimal environmental impact. The openness of the Green Belt would be satisfactorily maintained and the restoration of the tennis courts would enhance sporting opportunities in the area. The development would not be likely to result in harm to local traffic and parking conditions as it is served by a number of modes of transport that provide sustainable access to the site, including public transport and the existing parking arrangements deter excessive car use. Subject to safeguarding conditions that are recommended, there would not be harmful impacts on the local environment, including the living conditions of nearby residents. 
The development therefore complies with the relevant policies of the Development Plan, including ENV-B.1.1 (New Development), ENV-N.1.1 (Purposes of Including Land In and Objectives for the Use of Land in the Green Belt), ENV-N.1.3 (Acceptable Development in the Green Belt), ENV-B.1.5 (Environmental Improvements), ENV-P.1.7 (Light Pollution), C.1.3 (Existing Social and Community Facilities), C.4.3 (Physica
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

Condition : 3 - No development shall take place until samples of the materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.  Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Condition : 4 - The use hereby permitted shall not be begun until details of the arrangements for storing of waste and recycled materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The arrangements for storing of waste and recycled materials shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with any approval given and shall be completed before any part of the accommodation hereby permitted is occupied.

Condition : 5 - No development shall take place until full details of hard and soft landscape works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and works shall be carried out as approved before any part of the accommodation hereby permitted is occupied. Details shall include means of enclosure, boundary fencing/walls, external lighting, vehicle and pedestrian access areas, planting plans and specifications and an implementation programme.

Condition : 6 - In this condition "retained tree" means an existing tree which is to be retained in accordance with the approved plans and particulars; and paragraphs (a) and (b) below shall have effect until the expiration of (5 years?) from (the date of the occupation of the building for its permitted use).

(a) No retained tree shall be cut down, uprooted or destroyed, nor shall any retained tree be topped or lopped other than in accordance with the approved plans and particulars, without the written approval of the local planning authority.  Any topping or lopping approved shall be carried out in accordance with British Standard [BS 3998:1989].

(b) If any retained tree is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, another tree shall be planted at the same place and that tree shall be of such size and species, and shall be planted at such time, as may be specified in writing by the local planning authority.

(c) The erection of fencing for the protection of any retained tree shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plans and particulars before any equipment, machinery or materials are brought on to the site for the purposes of the development, and shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed from the site.  Nothing shall be stored or placed in any area fenced in accordance with this condition and the ground levels within those areas shall not be altered, nor shall any excavation be made, without the written consent of the local planning authority.

Condition : 7 - No fans, louvres, ducts or other external plant shall be installed without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority. All plant shall be designed to achieve a level of 10dB below the existing LA90 background noise level at 3.5m from the fa?ade of the nearest residences or commercial property.

Condition : 8 - No demolition or construction work shall take place on the site except between the hours of 8:00am to 6:00pm o Mondays to Fridays, 9:00am to 1:00pm on Saturdays, with no work to take place on Sundays and Bank Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority. No development shall take place until a Construction Logistics Plan has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. 

Information on Construction Logistics Plans is available at: http://www.tfl.gov.uk/businessandpartners/freight/11422.aspx.

Condition : 9 - No development shall take place until details of a Sustainable Drainage Scheme, including measures for living roofs and/or walls, harvesting of rainwater, the minimisation of water run-off from the site, aiming for greenfield levels, and the conservation and reuse as appropriate of other water supplies in the building have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall be carried out as approved prior to the occupation of the first floor extension hereby approved.

Condition : 10 - No development shall take place until details have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority, for a gas fired combined heat and power system (capacity of at least 80kW electricity) to serve the energy and heating needs of the development. The details shall be carried out as approved.

Condition : 12 - No development shall take place until full details of the lift access to the first floor, including its means of control, and circulation routes between the car park, tennis courts and main building, are submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall be carried out as approved.

Condition : 13 - No development shall take place until details have be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority for a scheme of acoustic insulation to ensure the maximum noise level to be permitted within the library with windows shut and any other necessary means of ventilation provided shall not exceed the "good" limits contained in BS8233:1999. These being LAeq,16hour = 40 dB.  The details shall be carried out as approved.

Condition : 14 - The floodlighting of the tennis courts hereby approved shall not be used except between 10:00am to 10:00pm on Monday to Saturday, and to 6:00pm on Sundays and Public Holidays, with the lights to be switched off automatically outside these those times.

Condition : 15 - Details of automatic timing, lux levels, lamps, direction and screening of floodlighting of the tennis courts, and exterior lighting of the building, car park and its curtilage, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the use tennis courts hereby permitted commences.  Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Condition : 16 - No amplified music shall be played and no other amplified noise (announcements/ tannoy) shall be made, outside of the building hereby approved.

Condition : 17 - No development shall take place until a Delivery and Servicing Plan has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Information on Delivery and Servicing Plans is available at: http://www.tfl.gov.uk/businessandpartners/freight/11423.aspx

Condition : 18 - Before the development hereby permitted commences:
a. The site shall be investigated by a competent person to identify the extent and nature of contamination. A detailed site investigation report shall be prepared and submitted to the Local Planning Authority (LPA). The report should include a tiered risk assessment of the contamination based on the proposed end use of the site.  Additional investigation may be required where it is deemed necessary.
b. If required, a scheme for decontamination of the site shall be submitted to the LPA, for written approval.  The scheme must account for any comments made by the LPA .

Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied:
c. The LPA shall be notified immediately if additional contamination is discovered during the course of the development. A competent person shall assess the additional contamination, and shall submit appropriate amendments to the scheme for decontamination in writing to the LPA for approval.  
d. The agreed scheme for decontamination, including amendments, must be fully implemented and a written validation (closure) report submitted to the LPA for approval."

Condition : 19 - A programme of management for the existing and proposed row of evergreen trees (Leylandii) between the tennis courts and the rear of residential properties along Uxbridge Road shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the refurbished tennis courts are used. This programme shall aim to protect the long term health of the trees and the effectiveness of their screening whilst not unduly blocking light to neighbouring gardens.

Refurbishment and floodlighting of the existing tennis courts and upgrading of landscape and carpark area
